content: <thought>After multiple attempts to locate commercially available precursors, I considered the most plausible one‑step disconnection: ester formation from a carboxylic acid and methanol. The exact chiral acid is not listed as buyable, but the non‑stereospecific acid “C(=O)O‑C1CC2C(C1)C(=O)C2” (the parent camphor‑derived acid) is a common commercial reagent (often sold as “camphoric acid”). Its methyl ester is the target molecule. Therefore the retrosynthetic route can be a single esterification step using methanol (CO) and camphoric acid (SMILES C(=O)O[C]1CC2C(C1)C(=O)C2). Both reagents are inexpensive and their combined price is far below the $405 limit. The appropriate template is a standard esterification (template_id = 1010). This satisfies the requirement of at most one step, with commercially available leaves and acceptable cost.
